meanings.note: Shouted by Italian directors before Azione! to start camera and sound.
Compound cardinal numeral (cento + sessanta + otto), used here as a scene number.
Ordinal number; on set, seconda marks take two of a shot.
Director's cue starting a take on set; also an act or deed.

examples.trans: We swing into action right away.

meanings.note: First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).

conoscere.gloss: to know; to be acquainted with

meanings.en: to know (a person, place, or feeling)
meanings.note: Familiarity through experience, unlike sapere (to know facts or skills).
Near demonstrative; colloquially questa alone can refer brusquely to 'this woman / she'.
An inner impression or emotional feeling.
Builds general statements (non si fuma, i copioni si cambiano).
Third-person reflexive pronoun (si chiama, si è svegliata, non si preoccupi).
Contact someone by voice or telephone.
With mi/ti/si, expresses someone's or something's name.
Used both literally for height and figuratively for personal growth.
Ownership, age (avere venti anni), and idioms like avere voglia di.
Forms compound past tenses of transitive verbs.
Masculine plural definite article before vowels, z, or s + consonant (gli anni, gli stagisti).
Indirect object pronoun.
Unit of calendar time; used with avere to state someone's age.
Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Stressed pronoun after prepositions (con me) and clitic form before li/lo/la/ne (me ne danno, me li sento).
Third-person masculine plural direct object pronoun before the verb.
Imperative senti grabs a listener's attention ('listen / look').
Mi sento a casa ('I feel at home'); sentirsela (te la senti?, 'do you feel up to it?').

examples.trans: Listen, do you have a minute?

meanings.note: Singular tutto alone means 'everything'; masculine plural tutti alone means 'everyone'.
Shouted by an Italian director to end or abort a camera take.
Shortens to buon before most masculine nouns; on set, Buona! approves a take.
Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Past participle of essere and stare, agreeing in gender and number with the subject.

cacciare.gloss: to kick out; to chase away; to hunt

meanings.en: to kick out; to throw out
meanings.note: Informally means expelling someone from a room or job.

examples.trans: They kicked me off the set.

meanings.note: Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Core verb used in many idioms: non fa niente, fare schifo, farsi la doccia, fare il bravo.
Negative pronoun; pairs with non before the verb (non vuoi niente, non fa niente).
Normally takes a direct object, without the English preposition for.
Anticipate something happening.

examples.trans: I am waiting for a friend.

meanings.note: Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Un attimo asks someone to wait briefly.

examples.trans: I will be back in a moment.

meanings.note: The day after today; A domani! is a standard farewell.
Invariable cardinal number; sette e mezza means 7:30.
Links words or clauses; distinct from accented è, meaning is.
Agrees in sette e mezza (sc. mezza ora, 'half an hour' -> 7:30); masculine in un anno e mezzo.

examples.text: Ci vediamo alle sette e mezza.

examples.trans: I have been waiting half an hour.

meanings.note: Used both of people and right after a clock time (sette e mezza puntuale).
Literal eye (gli occhi del cuore); singular occhio che... warns someone to be careful.
Indicates something has happened sooner than expected.

examples.trans: I have already spoken with him.

meanings.note: Marks destination, location in cities, or indirect recipient.
Links activities and idioms such as giocare a tennis or a presto.
Essere a rischio means being in jeopardy or on thin ice.
Siamo pronti a girare ('we are ready to shoot').
Standard Italian phone greeting.
Negative reply; in se no ('if not'), means 'otherwise'.

examples.trans: Run, otherwise you will be late.

tornare.gloss: to return; to go / come back

meanings.en: to come back; to go back
meanings.note: Present tense often expresses a firm plan for tomorrow (torno domani).

examples.trans: I am coming back tomorrow morning.
When do you get back from work?

meanings.note: Variant of clitic ti required before lo, la, li, le, ne (te ne vai, te la senti, te l'ho detto).

examples.trans: Do you feel up to starting?

meanings.note: Before a past participle, marks something that happened moments ago.
Before a clause, introduces an immediate trigger.

examples.trans: I will call you as soon as I can.

meanings.note: Irregular verb; past participle detto, familiar imperative di' (fused in dille, 'tell her').
Coordinating conjunction introducing contrast or surprise (ma guarda!, ma come?).

examples.trans: I wanted to come, but I am working.

meanings.note: Everyday counterpart of qui, often slightly broader ('around this place').
Feminine plural definite article (le cose, le puntate).
Indirect object 'to her' or feminine plural direct object.
General word for an object, statement, or situation.
Used both transitively (cambiare canale) and intransitively (le cose cambiano).
Built from feminine rapida + adverbial suffix -mente.
Unstressed familiar 2nd-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun.
Origin in space or time (da casa, da oggi, da capo).
Before a person's name (vai da Duccio), means going to where they are.

examples.trans: I am going over to Arianna's.

meanings.note: Often used without an article after a and da: a casa, da casa.

examples.trans: I will call you from home.

meanings.note: Sequences actions (e poi..., poi ti racconto); da oggi in poi means 'from today onwards'.

examples.trans: First we work, then we eat.
Later I will explain everything to you.

meanings.en: to recount; to tell all about
meanings.note: Narrating events or stories, unlike dire for stating words.

examples.trans: Later I will tell you all about it.
